apps.summary: Google Maps gives you directions and local search, and needs your location to do it. Google's Play Store label says Maps doesn't share your data with other companies; it lists approximate location, searches in the app and device IDs among data Google uses for "Advertising or marketing", and precise location for running and personalizing the app. Google has paid settlements to US states over its location tracking.

risk_tag_notes.ad_profiling: Google's own advertising; Google says Maps doesn't share data with other companies

apps.privacy_controls: In your Google Account: Location History, which powers Timeline in Maps, and Web & App Activity. Google said in 2023 that Timeline would be saved on your device.

consequences.text: Google's Play Store label says Maps doesn't share your data with other companies. It lists web browsing history among the data Maps collects, for advertising or marketing.
consequences.wording: According to Google's Play Store data safety label, read 2026-10-04.

sources.quote: doesn't share user data with other companies … Web browsing history Advertising or marketing

consequences.text: Google's privacy policy says it doesn't share your personal information with companies, organizations or individuals outside Google, except in cases the policy lists, such as with your consent.
consequences.wording: According to Google's privacy policy dated 2026-10-01.

sources.title: Google Privacy Policy

consequences.text: Google said in December 2023 that Timeline in Maps, which is powered by the Location History setting, would be saved on your device, with backups to the cloud optional and encrypted.
consequences.wording: According to Google's blog post of 2023-12-12.

sources.quote: Timeline … powered by a setting called Location History … saved right on your device
